page: Microsoft Azure FX64-32mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. This instance is equipped with 1344.0 GB of RAM, translating to 42.0 GB of memory per physical core. Local storage consists of a 3780 GB disk, and the server supports Premium Storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaching 241.54 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 136.66 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. Geekbench single-core performance is in the top 10% with a score of 2367.0, while the multi-core score of 18564.0 falls in the top 25%. Single-threaded gzip compression at 34.58 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.31 GB/sec also rank in the top 25%. However, multi-core stress-ng CPU performance at 35522.79 and Passmark database operations at 20191.25 remain in the middle 50% tier.

The server demonstrates a clear performance tradeoff in large-scale machine learning tasks. While prompt processing for a medium 7B LLM model is strong at 186.74 tokens/sec, text generation for a large 70B model is weak, registering at 2.71 tokens/sec due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. Qualitatively, the high memory density and large local storage capacity provide high resource density for memory-bound enterprise applications. This hardware profile is suited for large in-memory databases, memory-intensive data processing, and enterprise workloads requiring high memory-to-vCPU ratios.
